area: Adversarial review of the deferred-findings spec for agentskills issue #120 (harness errexit lock in scripts/test_account_workflows.py; the unguarded-command count comment in .github/workflows/account-skill-zips.yml)

findings.claim: SPEC DEFECT, most serious. The spec's whole shape taxonomy rests on a false bash premise: it classifies the two echoes on the right-hand side of a `||` (lines 209, 228) as 'guarded', in a paragraph whose entire subject is which commands errexit acts on. Errexit is suppressed only for commands BEFORE the final `&&`/`||` in a list; the command FOLLOWING the final `||` is fully subject to errexit. So an `echo` on a `||` RHS aborts the step on failure exactly like a bare one. Three downstream consequences: (1) FINDING 4's headline diagnosis ('it included the guarded pyyaml fallback while omitting a bare echo — two errors cancelling') is wrong — 228 is NOT guarded, so including it was correct on the paragraph's own dimension, and the shipped comment's real error is that it omits TWO echoes (209 and 307), not that it swaps one for another. The 'other echoes equally exposed to errexit' set is 14, not 12. (2) The proposed replacement comment bakes the false claim in permanently: 'apart from the two that are the `||` fallback of a `mkdir` or a `pip install` and are covered by that list rather than for their own sake' — they are not covered; if either echo fails the step aborts. (3) The proposed comment then re-states the wrong diagnosis as durable prose ('it said twelve and then named a twelve that included the guarded `pyyaml` fallback'). The spec would replace a comment with a wrong enumeration by a comment with a wrong explanation of bash, which is precisely the 'a wrong tolerance comment is worse than none' standard the paragraph exists to hold.
findings.evidence:
$ cat e1.sh
set -uo pipefail
mkdir -p /proc/nope \
  || { echo "fallback ran"; false; }
echo "REACHED-AFTER"
$ bash -e e1.sh
mkdir: cannot create directory '/proc/nope': No such file or directory
fallback ran
exit=1        <- REACHED-AFTER never printed: errexit fired inside the `||` RHS group

Isolating the echo itself (stdout closed makes echo fail):
$ printf 'false || echo hi >&-\necho "REACHED" >&2\n' > e5.sh ; bash -e e5.sh
e5.sh: line 1: echo: write error: Bad file descriptor
exit=1        <- REACHED not printed
$ printf 'echo hi >&-\necho "REACHED" >&2\n' > e6.sh ; bash -e e6.sh
e6.sh: line 1: echo: write error: Bad file descriptor
exit=1        <- identical behaviour for the bare echo

POSIX/bash errexit exemption list: '...any command executed in a && or || list except the command following the final && or ||'. Both 209 and 228 ARE that final command.

The two lines, verbatim at HEAD:
  208  `            mkdir -p ../eval-results \`
  209  `              || echo "no placeholder for the missing eval-results clone either; the annotation below covers it"`
  227  `          python3 -m pip install --quiet pyyaml==6.0.3 \`
  228  `            || { pip_ok=no; echo "::warning::pyyaml install failed; unless it is already present the verdict will be unavailable"; }`
(echo is the LAST command of the `{ }` group, so the group's status is the echo's.)
findings.proposedChange:
Drop the guarded/bare split from both the analysis and the replacement comment. The true invariant is: every `echo` in this step is equally exposed to errexit — the two on a `||` RHS included — and they are all left unguarded because an `echo` to a runner's stdout essentially never fails; the one that also REDIRECTS is the one named above, and redirection is what makes it failable. Replacement text for lines 165-173 (8-space indent):

        # THE QUALIFIER IS LOAD-BEARING, because an unqualified claim here
        # would be false and this paragraph's own argument is that a wrong
        # tolerance comment is worse than none. Every OTHER `echo` in this
        # step is unguarded too, and errexit acts on all of them - including
        # the two that sit on the right-hand side of a `||`, which protects
        # the `mkdir` and the `pip install` on its LEFT and does nothing for
        # the `echo` that follows it: the command after the final `||` is the
        # one command in the list that errexit is NOT exempted from. They are
        # all left that way because an `echo` to a runner's stdout essentially
        # never fails; the one that also REDIRECTS is the one named above, and
        # redirection is what makes it failable.
        #
        # NO COUNT HERE, DELIBERATELY. There was one and it was wrong: it
        # named twelve echoes and there are fourteen, omitting the `mkdir`
        # fallback and the `no verdict, which follows from the clone failure`
        # line. The number is not stable either - it moved inside the branch
        # that wrote it, when the empty-capture guard grew a third arm - and
        # nothing in the repo asserts it, so it reads as checked while going
        # stale on the next edit. The SHAPE is the durable claim.

Lock it, or it rots the same way: a test over the parsed audit-step body asserting that no line matching `^\s*echo\b` (after `code()`) carries a redirect except the `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` write — that is checkable, unlike a count.

findings.claim: SPEC DEFECT in EDIT 3/EDIT 4. Replacing `[bash, "-e", script, verdict]` with `runner_argv(script, verdict)` orphans the nine-line comment directly above it that exists solely to explain that literal argv, and the spec proposes no edit for it. Lines 649-657 are titled '`-e`, BECAUSE THAT IS THE SHELL THE STEP ACTUALLY GETS' and lines 658-659 say '`verdict` is $1 of the SCRIPT, so it is passed straight after the path - there is no `-c` placeholder $0 to absorb an argument'. After EDIT 3 neither `-e` nor the argument position is visible at the call site, so both paragraphs describe something the reader can no longer see. In a repo whose whole thesis is that a comment describing code the reader cannot check is the defect, EDIT 2-4 manufacture one. The spec's open question raises 'one more indirection between the reader and /usr/bin/bash -e {0}' as an aesthetic preference and never notices there is concrete existing prose that goes stale.
findings.evidence:
$ sed -n '649,667p' scripts/test_account_workflows.py
        # `-e`, BECAUSE THAT IS THE SHELL THE STEP ACTUALLY GETS. The workflow
        # declares no `shell:` and no `defaults:`, so GitHub runs every `run:`
        # body as `/usr/bin/bash -e {0}`, and the step's own `set -uo pipefail`

        # `verdict` is $1 of the SCRIPT, so it is passed straight after the

        script = _script(...)
        proc = subprocess.run(
            [bash, "-e", script, verdict],

findings.proposedChange: Either (a) drop EDIT 2-4 entirely — EDIT 1 is the lock and passes without them (verified below) and the literal argv is what the surrounding prose is written against; or (b) if the helper goes in, move lines 649-657 into `runner_argv`'s docstring and shorten the call-site comment to one line pointing at it, and reword 658-659 to describe `runner_argv(script, verdict)`'s `*args` rather than 'straight after the path'. Do not land EDIT 3/4 with 649-659 untouched.

findings.claim: SPEC OVERSTATEMENT. FINDING 1(b) says the 2x2 shows '`-e` is the single thing standing between the shipped guard and a silent green', but the sabotage it uses — the bare `mkdir` at line 208 — lives in the step HEAD, which only `_run_step` executes (`_tail()` starts at the heredoc's `) || verdict=""`). The matrix therefore exercises `_run_step`'s `-e` and never touches `_run`'s. Measured on the shipped tree, dropping `-e` from `_run` ALONE reds nothing: no test in the tail family depends on errexit at all. The lock is still right on fidelity grounds, but the evidence offered does not support the generalisation, and a reader who trusts it will believe line 667's `-e` is currently protecting a test.

$ python3 -m pytest scripts/test_account_workflows.py -q ; echo EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
56 passed in 1.74s
EXIT=0

For contrast, `_run_step`'s `-e` with the bare-mkdir regression applied (spec's row 3, reproduced exactly):

  1 failed, 55 passed   EXIT=1
and row 4 (no -e, bare mkdir): 56 passed, EXIT=0.

Source of the asymmetry, scripts/test_account_workflows.py:608 — `_tail()` returns `body[body.index(marker) + len(marker):]`, i.e. everything from the heredoc's `) || verdict=""` onward; the `mkdir` at workflow line 208 is above that marker.
findings.proposedChange: Reword FINDING 1(b) to what was measured: '`-e` is the single thing standing between the shipped guard in the step HEAD and a silent green; `_run`'s `-e` currently guards no test and is held for fidelity alone.' Keep the lock on both spawns — a fidelity invariant is exactly the kind that should be asserted before a regression needs it — but say which half is load-bearing today so the next reader does not delete the other half believing a test covers it.

findings.claim: SOUND, reproduced independently — EDIT 1 is a real lock and I could not defeat it. Inserted verbatim at line 1280 it passes on the shipped tree and reds on all three ways `-e` can go missing. openQuestions: The corrected errexit reading changes what the audit step actually guarantees, not just what the comment says: line 209's `echo` and line 228's `{ pip_ok=no; echo ...; }` will abort the step if the echo fails, on the exact path where the eval-results clone or the pyyaml install already failed. That is the degradation path the whole step exists to keep alive. Is it worth making those two `|| { ...; } || :`-safe, or is 'echo to a runner's stdout never fails' good enough there too? I lean good enough, but the decision should be recorded rather than absorbed into a comment rewrite.

The spec's fallback proposal — 'assert that every NON-echo command sits in an `if` condition or a `||` list' — is described more confidently than it can be built. At HEAD the audit body's non-echo commands include `set -uo pipefail` (175), eight bare assignments (195/196/201/207/226/305 and the flag sets), and `: ;;` (436), none of which sit in either shape. Any such test needs a carve-out list roughly as long as the thing it asserts. The checkable invariant is narrower: no `echo` carries a redirect except the `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` write, and every command SUBSTITUTION or external command is in an `if` condition or a `||` list.

Should the fidelity rule be stated once, in the repo, rather than re-derived per harness? Three separate comment blocks (workflow lines 149-173, test file 649-657, test file 759-761) each explain that GitHub hands a `run:` body to `/usr/bin/bash -e {0}` and that `set -o` cannot take it back. That is the shape AGENTS.md says belongs in one place; the spec adds a fourth copy in the new docstring.

scripts/test_account_workflows.py:1319 and :1367 spawn `bash -c` with no `-e` against a `case` fragment lifted out of record-account-upload.yml, which I confirmed runs under the runner's `bash -e`. Those tests assert only the exit code of a guard, so `-e` probably does not change their verdict — but nobody has measured it, and _script()'s own docstring argues at length that `-c` is the wrong execution mode. Worth an issue, not worth blocking this one.

Issue #120 items 2 and 3 remain untouched and I did not look at them. Item 2 (`_case_statuses` off `body.index`) is adjacent to the parse-don't-scan reasoning EDIT 1 leans on, so whoever closes item 1 should read item 2 before choosing a shape.
